title: BBC Staff Raise Concerns About Director-General’s Praise For AI-Generated ‘Doctor Who’
key_facts: At a BBC staff town hall on Wednesday (7 Oct 2026), employees raised concerns about Director-General Matt Brittin's comments on an AI-generated Doctor Who episode.
Brittin had said at the Royal Television Society London Convention last week that the AI Doctor Who was "pretty good".
One question drew 86 upvotes, asking him to rethink his "fascination with AI-generated programmes" and noting Doctor Who is made in Cardiff.
Another asked whether the BBC should fully reject generative AI.
Brittin said he was making a point about the pace of change, that "humans are leading", and that the BBC must understand AI risks to journalistic integrity.
Deadline separately reports producers bidding to reboot Doctor Who for the BBC.
quote_evidence: During a staff town hall on Wednesday, BBC insiders voiced concerns about Brittin’s comments at the Royal Television Society London Convention last week, in which the director-general said that an AI Doctor Who was “pretty good.”
“But I want to be really clear: Humans are leading, and I believe in human creativity, enhanced by whatever tools.”
why_it_matters_hint: Staff pushback at a public broadcaster over generative AI in programme-making.
event_date: 7 Oct 2026 (town hall); remarks at RTS convention the week before
